_comment: Catalogue for the Test simulations view. Each entry starts from the mode's
own defaults (GET /api/defaults/{mode}) and applies `overrides` on top, so an
entry only has to state what it changes. Paths are dotted paths into the
setup model; unknown paths are reported rather than silently ignored.
This file is served as a static asset and is deliberately NOT part of the
qpsim source manifest, so editing the catalogue costs no recertification.

groups.title: Fixed points
groups.hint: Undriven cases whose answer is known ahead of the run.

cases.title: Thermal equilibrium
cases.summary: No drive, phonons pinned at the bath. The collision integral vanishes at f = f_FD(T_bath), so the solve should return the thermal distribution.
cases.expect: x_qp at its thermal value for 0.2 K; the solver should converge almost immediately.

cases.title: Thermal equilibrium, cold
cases.summary: The same fixed point at 0.1 K, where the pair channel is suppressed by e^(-2Δ/kT) and the number mode becomes hard to resolve in float64.
cases.expect: Same qualitative answer, far smaller x_qp. This is the regime where amplitude convergence gets delicate.

groups.title: Driven steady states
groups.hint: A drive balanced by recombination. These have a unique answer because the pair channel sets the amplitude.

cases.title: Sub-gap photon drive
cases.summary: A sub-gap drive redistributes quasiparticles in energy without creating them; recombination sets how many there are.
cases.expect: x_qp above thermal, with the distribution reshaped near the gap edge.

cases.title: Pair-breaking photon drive
cases.summary: An above-gap drive creates quasiparticles directly. Recombination is the only sink, so it alone fixes the steady state.
cases.expect: A markedly higher x_qp than the sub-gap case at comparable drive.

cases.title: Fixed bath vs. trapped phonons
cases.summary: The same drive with the phonons solved and a finite escape time, instead of pinned at the bath. Recombination phonons can now break pairs again before they leave.
cases.expect: Higher x_qp than the pinned-bath case: that difference is phonon trapping. Run this alongside 'Pair-breaking photon drive' to see it.

cases.title: Photon kick response
cases.summary: Start thermal, switch on a pair-breaking drive at t = 0, and watch f(E) climb to the driven steady state with the phonons frozen at the bath.
cases.expect: A monotone rise in x_qp that flattens onto the steady-state value the 0-D solver finds independently.

groups.title: Spatial transport
groups.hint: The dirty-limit operator is A1. The others are labelled diagnostics, not alternative physics.

cases.title: Uniform strip, A1
cases.summary: A uniform gap along the strip, so every energy diffuses independently at D_eff = D_0/N_1(E), falling toward the gap edge.
cases.expect: A smooth spatial profile with no gap-gradient drift: A1 carries none by construction.

cases.title: Same strip, legacy operator C
cases.summary: Identical to the uniform-strip case but with the clean/BRT closure. At a uniform gap C shares A1's rate and differs only in conserved density.
cases.expect: Very similar profile here; the two separate once the gap varies in space.

cases.title: Step gap interface
cases.summary: Two regions of unequal gap joined at one face. Quasiparticles collect on the low-gap side.
cases.expect: An asymmetric profile with a visible discontinuity in occupation across the step.

groups.title: Literature reproductions
groups.hint: These set up the CONDITIONS of a published point so you can see the physics and vary it. They are not the certified figure reproductions — those are full sweeps with pinned baselines and provenance, and they live in the validation suite rather than here.

cases.title: Fischer & Catelani 2023, Fig. 6 — one point
cases.summary: Table I aluminium parameters at T_bath = 0.20 K under the sub-gap drive, with the phonons solved at a finite escape time. This is the single operating point the Fig. 6 sweep is built from.
cases.expect: A driven steady state near the published operating point. The certified 66-point sweep, its pinned baseline and its evidence ladder are in the validation suite, not here.

cases.title: Marchegiani 2025 — parity switching
cases.summary: The junction rate-equation layer at its shipped defaults, which are the M25 parameter topology.
cases.expect: Parity-switching rates against the junction parameters.
